stops.note: Luigi Galvani of Bologna reported in 1791 that dissected frogs' legs twitched when touched with two different metals, which he took for 'animal electricity'
the Paris engineer Stanislas Sorel patented coating iron with zinc in 1837, 'galvanising' it against rust
in 1803 Galvani's nephew Giovanni Aldini made the corpse of executed murderer George Forster twitch in London; hence 'galvanise' as 'to jolt into action'

current_meaning: to shock or excite into action; to coat iron with zinc
